concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Edit the supplied Helmetd normal-riding HUD into one new state. Keep the landscape 16:9 composition, photographic rider-eye road scene, restrained white sans-serif type, pale cyan navigation, top-left helmetd wordmark, top-right Wi-Fi icon and 82% battery, and the existing fixed speed/gear location. Preserve the typography and visual family. All data are illustrative. The road is background context, not an additional camera feed. Keep most of the forward road unobstructed. Do not add glasses rims, helmet outlines, radar, crosshairs, neon sci-fi decorations, web menus, explanatory paragraphs or invented collision probabilities. A slim white presentation footer sits outside the HUD.
Primary request: REAR THREAT mode. Keep '32 mph', gear '3', and the existing left-turn navigation '800 ft / Oak Street', but make navigation slightly subdued.
Replace the normal right-edge camera icon and 'Voice ready' text with one contextual rear-camera inset in the lower-right quarter, about 27% image width and 23% height. Its crisp amber outline and type match the earlier restrained HUD. Inside it show a believable rear-facing camera picture: a dark SUV following in the same lane, the front of the SUV facing the rear camera, with a single thin amber bounding box around the SUV. The inset header reads exactly 'REAR CAMERA', with a tiny recording dot and 'Buffering'.
Immediately above the inset show a compact amber rear-direction chevron and the clear warning 'VEHICLE CLOSING'. Below it one short line reads 'Behind you'. This directional alert and camera inset are the only expanded elements; the forward roadway center stays clear. Keep a tiny microphone glyph only, without a conversational caption. No numeric vehicle distance, speed estimate, collision timer, or instruction to brake or steer.
Footer exact text: 'HELMETD / REAR THREAT' on the left and 'Motorcycle HUD concept' on the right. This is one realistic alert screen, not multiple panels.

Use case: ui-mockup. Edit the supplied Helmetd normal-riding HUD into one new state. Keep the landscape 16:9 composition, photographic rider-eye road scene, restrained white sans-serif type, pale cyan navigation, top-left helmetd wordmark, top-right Wi-Fi icon and 82% battery, and the existing fixed speed/gear location. Preserve the typography and visual family. All data are illustrative. The road is background context, not an additional camera feed. Keep most of the forward road unobstructed. Do not add glasses rims, helmet outlines, radar, crosshairs, neon sci-fi decorations, web menus, explanatory paragraphs or invented collision probabilities. A slim white presentation footer sits outside the HUD.
Primary request: ROAD HAZARD mode, a shared hazard report from another rider. Keep the original fixed '32 mph', gear '3', and top navigation '800 ft / Oak Street'.
Add one compact, very legible amber hazard notice in the lower-left quadrant, above the left camera symbol and away from the forward road center. Use a simple outlined warning triangle and the exact large title 'DEBRIS AHEAD'. Under it, two short lines read '300 ft · Rider report' and 'Reported 2 min ago'. Use a small location-pin icon if helpful, with only a short hairline divider. The notice floats directly over the scene without a large filled card.
This warning is based on a location report, so do NOT draw a detection box on the forward road, do not paint a route on the pavement, and do not add actual debris or claim the helmet's cameras see it. Keep both small side-camera glyphs; no camera inset. Replace the ordinary 'Voice ready' caption with a tiny microphone/speaker glyph so the hazard has priority. Preserve the calm, open look and keep all labels large enough to read.
Footer exact text: 'HELMETD / ROAD HAZARD' on the left and 'Motorcycle HUD concept' on the right.

Use case: ui-mockup. Edit the supplied Helmetd normal-riding image into a POSSIBLE CRASH COUNTDOWN DEMO state. Preserve the same landscape proportions, photographic road scene, small handlebar silhouette, restrained modern white sans-serif typography, helmetd wordmark at upper left, Wi-Fi and 82% battery upper right, and slim white presentation footer. This depicts a stationary, controlled demonstration; no actual collision, injured person, wreckage, emergency responder, or moving camera blur.
Replace the top-center route guidance with a compact rust-red warning triangle and the exact heading 'POSSIBLE CRASH'. Remove side-camera icons and the 'Voice ready' caption.
In the central lower half, make one very clear and simple countdown composition: the small line 'Report to Mac in', large digits '00:18', then a wide thin outlined control reading 'HOLD BUTTON TO CANCEL'. Below it one small status line reads 'Saving camera clips'. The timer and cancel action must be visually prominent and perfectly legible, with generous space, no surrounding giant opaque panel, and no distracting chart. The UI represents a proposed physical-button hold action, not a touch target on glasses.
In the original speed/gear location near the bottom, show '0 mph' and '— GEAR' in subdued white. Keep the scene center otherwise readable; the countdown may take focus because the vehicle is stationary.
Footer exact text: 'HELMETD / CRASH DEMO' at left and 'Report preview · No emergency call' at right.
No SOS dispatched label, no claim of contacting emergency services, no collision probability, no medical advice, no other numbers, no red full-screen flash, no neon sci-fi effects, no added explanatory paragraphs. Match the original product's quiet visual language while clearly showing a high-priority countdown.

Use case: ui-mockup. Edit the supplied Helmetd normal-riding image into a GROUP RIDING state. Preserve the same full-bleed rider-eye road photograph, restrained white sans-serif UI, pale cyan navigation, helmetd wordmark, Wi-Fi icon and 82% battery, fixed '32 mph' and '3 GEAR', and the top '800 ft / Oak Street' left-turn instruction.
Add a compact, beautifully aligned group-status cluster at the right edge above the lower-right camera glyph. It should occupy at most a quarter of the image width, float directly over the scene with almost no panel fill, and leave the entire road center open. Its heading is 'GROUP · 3 RIDERS'. Under one short hairline divider show two simple rows with a small initial/avatar circle and readable text: 'Riley' with '180 ft ahead', and 'Sam' with '420 ft behind'. Use white for ordinary data. Beneath these rows show one restrained amber indicator and 'Sam is falling behind'. Three riders includes the wearer, so list only these two other riders.
Do not attach labels to physical vehicles in the scene and do not draw world-anchored arrows: these are approximate group location readouts in a fixed HUD cluster. Remove the verbose 'Voice ready' line, leaving only a small microphone glyph unobtrusively at the lower right. Retain a small left camera icon. No camera windows, no map, no extra warning, no group chat messages, no huge avatar cards.
Footer exact text: 'HELMETD / GROUP RIDE' at left and 'Motorcycle HUD concept' at right.
Keep existing typography, icon line weight, photographic lighting, and comfortable negative space. Only the requested group cluster, voice treatment, and footer should change.

Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: high-fidelity flat desktop web-app screenshot for the Helmetd civic road-safety dashboard, wide landscape 16:9.
Primary request: design a polished and practical civic dashboard that turns aggregated motorcycle hazard and near-miss reports into a road-quality map. This is a separate Mac/web interface, not graphics inside glasses. Show the actual app viewport, not a device mockup, laptop, browser frame or scene photograph.
Style: restrained editorial data design, warm white and pale stone backgrounds, charcoal modern sans-serif typography, thin grey dividers, small amber and muted teal data accents. Excellent hierarchy, readable labels, careful alignment. Spacious and professional, with a large useful map dominating the composition. Avoid a grid of rounded statistic cards, glass effects, neon, and decorative gradients.
Structure: narrow left sidebar headed 'helmetd' with a small 'ROAD INSIGHTS' sublabel. Sidebar navigation exactly 'Overview', 'Hazards', 'Near misses', 'Road quality'; Overview is selected.
Top of main workspace: page title 'Road awareness', then small subtitle 'Aggregated rider reports'. On the right show two simple filter controls 'Demo district' and 'Last 7 days', and a small clearly legible badge 'Illustrative data'.
Beneath the title show a single flat horizontal metric strip divided by thin rules: '48 Reports', '12 Active hazards', '7 Near misses'. These are illustrative sample values.
Main area: a large muted street map of a fictional small district, with a simple rational street grid, park area and river, restrained road labels, several small amber pothole/hazard markers, and a few subdued teal translucent near-miss hotspot areas. Use anonymized aggregate markers only; no individual rider dots or routes. Put a compact map legend 'Hazards' and 'Near-miss hotspots' in a corner.
A fixed right detail rail contains one selected record: heading 'Pothole', location 'Oak St & 3rd Ave', then clean labeled rows 'Reports  6', 'Confidence  High', 'Severity  Moderate', 'Last report  12 min ago'. A small secondary line reads 'Community reports · Not inspected'. A modest outlined action reads 'Review reports'. Below a divider show a short two-row list headed 'Nearby reports': 'Debris · Pine Road' and 'Construction · River Ave'.
The bottom edge of the map area can include a slim, simple 7-bar spark chart labeled 'Reports this week'; no dense axes needed.
Constraints: flat product UI with impeccably readable text, no marketing headlines, no fake photos, no real-city claim, no emergency dispatch controls, no 3D map perspective, no random tiny text, no developer/debug chrome, no watermarks. This is an illustrative product concept.

selected_correction.prompt: Make one targeted typographic edit to the supplied rear-threat HUD screenshot. Completely redraw the narrow header row INSIDE the amber-bordered rear camera inset at the lower right. The left side of that header must read 'REAR CAMERA'. The right side must contain a tiny amber recording dot followed by exactly three uppercase letters: 'REC'. Erase the old word 'Buffering' completely; none of its letters may remain. This is an exact text replacement, not a stylistic suggestion. Preserve the camera picture, SUV detection box, inset border, all other HUD labels, road background, navigation, speed, gear, and footer unchanged. Do not use the word Recording or Buffering anywhere in the finished image.
